subject: Insurance
title: The Slavery Insurance Scandal
description: A quick, practical guide to The Slavery Insurance Scandal.

hook.text: Lloyd's of London insured slave ships and their 'cargo.' Human beings were listed as insurable property on policies.

buildup.text: Slave traders insured against losses from drowning, disease, and rebellion.

discovery.text: The Zong massacre of 1781 saw enslaved people thrown overboard so owners could claim insurance. Murder for profit.

twist.text: In 2020, Lloyd's formally apologized for its role.

climax.text: Insurance is a tool. It can enable the best of trade—or the worst of human exploitation. The tool has no morals.

punchline.text: Insured as cargo. Insurance funded the slave trade's worst crimes.

quiz.question: What did the Zong massacre demonstrate about insurance?
options: Insurance could incentivize murder for financial claims
